description: Figure 5 is a grouped bar chart illustrating the performance gain (in percentage) achieved by VisuoThink through predictive rollout search, calculated as the performance gap between VisuoThink with and without rollout search. The horizontal axis displays three large vision-language model (LVLM) architectures: GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, and Qwen2-72B-VL. The vertical axis represents “Performance Gain (+%)”, scaled from 0 to 30 in increments of 5. For each model, two bars are shown: one for “Strong Supervision” (hatched purple) and one for “Weak Supervision” (solid light purple), as indicated by the legend. For GPT-4o, strong supervision yields approximately 24% gain, while weak supervision yields about 5%. For Claude-3.5-Sonnet, strong supervision results in roughly 9% gain, and weak supervision in about 3%. For Qwen2-72B-VL, strong supervision achieves approximately 15% gain, and weak supervision about 5%. Across all three models, the performance gain under strong supervision is substantially higher than under weak supervision, visually supporting the paper’s claim that predictive rollouts are more effective when stronger supervisory signals are available.
